messages:
maria: secbot alerted on a historical commit in `infra/monorepo` that contains a KMS-encrypted blob that looks like a service-account private key wrapped and checked in. :rotating_light:
secbot: automated-detect: high-confidence match on pattern `ENCRYPTED_KEY_v1` in commit 9f3a2b (2019-06-21). raw snippet:
```
commit 9f3a2b
file: tools/ci/creds.enc
match: -----BEGIN ENCRYPTED KEY-----ABCDEF...-----END ENCRYPTED KEY-----
```
ben: ack. tagging infra. this is probably the old CI service account we migrated off in 2021. we should assume key compromised until proven otherwise. :lock:
sasha: timeline? do we have any usage records for that key recently?
ben: quick check: IAM console shows that key-id `0123456789abcdef` was rotated and then removed 2021-10, but there are archived build logs in gs://redwood-ci-archives/ that contain deploy job envs from 2019-2021. will check access logs for any usage after removal.
maria: immediate containment plan: 1) revoke any remaining SA keys for ci-service@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com 2) rotate KMS key used to wrap blobs 3) revoke any long-lived tokens referenced in archived logs 4) notify legal/compliance. can infra run revocation now? :eyes:
ben: running revocation now. command I'm going to run:
```bash
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=ci-service@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json
# then for each key id:
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=ci-service@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --quiet
```
ben: also creating an IAM deny policy on that service account until we confirm no active workloads. will also rotate the KMS key used for envelope encryption: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key <key> --location=...` and then update decrypt permissions.
tom: quick question — if the blob is KMS-wrapped, rotating the KMS key won't make the leaked wrapped blob decryptable if attacker has access to old KMS key; we should schedule destruction of old key versions if allowed by policy. legal: we may need to preserve them for forensics, check retention windows.
legal: agree — preserve forensic images. legal wants a copy of original blob and access logs preserved in a WORM location before destruction. we can provide controlled copies to the IR team.
sasha: regarding repo cleanup: do we rewrite history and force-push to remove the blob? that will be disruptive for forks and refs. alternatives: leave history + add repo-level notice + rotate creds + block PRs referencing old commits. thoughts?
maria: IR recommendation: do both in phases. phase 1 = containment + rotate/revoke + block pushes to protected branches that reference the commit; phase 2 (after comms) = repo history rewrite using `git filter-repo` to remove the blob from all branches/refs, then force-push org-wide. must coordinate with platform to update mirrors and tag owners.
ben: proposed git filter-repo command (dry-run first):
```bash
git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/infra.git
git filter-repo --invert-paths --path tools/ci/creds.enc --force
# verify missing blob, then push --mirror back to origin (coordinated blackout window)
git push --mirror origin
```
sasha: concern: loss of commit SHAs breaks CI and pinned SHAs in other repos. we need a list of dependent repos and a rollback plan. I'll run a search for references to the old commit id `9f3a2b` across our org.
maria: action items:
- ben: revoke keys + deny SA (ASAP, in progress)
- ben: archive preserved copy to secure-forensics bucket (complete after revocation)
- sasha: map repo dependents + schedule rewrite window (ETA 6h)
- legal: confirm retention/forensics constraints (ETA 2h)
- maria: public/ops comms draft for internal channels and customer-facing if needed (ETA 4h)
secbot: incident-ticket created: #IR-2027-089 (link: https://incidents.internal.redwood/IR-2027-089) assigned to eng-security and infra.
ben: revocation done: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=ci-service@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --quiet` — no recent usage found post-2021 in Cloud Audit Logs. archived build logs have restricted access now.
sasha: found a handful of repos referencing the old commit via submodule pins (4 repos). I'll open PRs to update pins to latest stable commits and coordinate force-push timing.
maria: for CI logs in GCS, we need to scrub env var dumps that contain tokens. ben: can you list objects with `creds.enc` in name and move to forensics bucket, then create a redaction job to redact plaintext appearances?
ben: moving objects to gs://secure-forensics/IR-2027-089/ now. redaction scheduled; note: we cannot alter historical GCP audit logs, so we'll preserve those.
tom: follow-up: add a preventive rule to our pre-receive hook to detect `ENCRYPTED KEY` patterns and block commits with any blob larger than 4KB in `tools/ci`. also add a repo-scanning scheduled job to run weekly.
maria: agree. afterwrap items: create pre-receive rule, update onboarding docs about never checking keys, and add KMS envelope encryption rotation checklist to runbooks.
legal: we will coordinate any external disclosure if evidence of exfiltration is found. for now, treat as contained incident.
maria: thanks all. summary will be pushed to #incidents and I'll post an internal postmortem draft in 48h. :thumbsup:
